candidates.title: Live fs::copy of a WAL database is not a consistent backup
candidates.rationale: Store::open at line 60 calls `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` before `fs::copy` at line 62. The checkpoint reduces but does not eliminate the WAL race: a concurrent writer (another Store instance) could append WAL frames between checkpoint and copy. However, the architecture ensures Store is !Sync and only one instance writes at a time, making the race narrow. The backup is best-effort and logged as such (line 63 warns on failure).
candidates.counterevidence: The copy runs during migration only (preexisting DB with current < LATEST_VERSION). Normal operation never hits this path. The comment says 'best-effort' explicitly. WAL checkpoint(TRUNCATE) does fold most pending data. The catalog is rebuildable from JSONL, so even a corrupted backup is recoverable.
candidates.remaining_check: Would need concurrent write load test to confirm race window size
candidates.original_candidate_title: 1. Live `fs::copy` of a WAL database is not a consistent backup
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `Store::open` (`sqlite_store.rs`, preexisting + `current < LATEST_VERSION`) runs best-effort `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` (return value discarded), then `std::fs::copy(path, path.with_extension("sqlite.bak"))` of the main file only, while `conn` is already open. It does not use `VACUUM INTO`, the backup API, or copy `-wal`/`-shm`.

candidates.title: No fsync/sync_all after JSONL append — power-loss can lose tail events
candidates.rationale: The writer calls `file.flush()` (line 267, 307) but never `sync_all()` or `sync_data()`. On NTFS/APFS, a flush pushes data to the OS page cache but does not guarantee disk persistence. A power loss between flush and OS writeback can lose the last few events. This is a real gap in crash durability.
candidates.counterevidence: The JSONL is append-only and each line is a complete JSON event. A partial write is detected by the indexer (serde_json parse failure on last line → skipped). Loss is bounded to the tail of the current session. The catalog is a projection that can re-index surviving data. sync_all on every event would significantly degrade throughput.
candidates.remaining_check: None — mechanism confirmed; impact bounded by append-only + skip-bad-line design
candidates.original_candidate_title: 2. `transaction()` is DEFERRED; two catalog writers can hit `SQLITE_BUSY` with no retry
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `replace_session`, `delete_session`, `approve_candidate` all use `self.conn.transaction()` (rusqlite default `BEGIN` / DEFERRED). `open` sets `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 2000` only. Comment in `Store::open` admits stop-session indexer and archive-open sweep write concurrently. There is no `transaction_with_behavior(Immediate)`, no retry/backoff, and no mapping of `ErrorCode::DatabaseBusy` to a retryable type.

candidates.title: Retention prunes JSONL files but catalog rows persist — ghost sessions
candidates.rationale: Retention (KEEP_LAST_SESSIONS=100, MAX_TOTAL_BYTES=500MB) deletes old JSONL files but does not delete their corresponding catalog rows. Re-indexing only processes surviving files, so pruned sessions' catalog rows become orphaned (no journal to verify them). These 'ghost' sessions still appear in the archive UI.
candidates.counterevidence: By design: catalog rows are 'additive and deliberate long-term history' (persistence/AGENTS.md). The user might want to see old session metadata even after journal files are pruned. A re-index from scratch would lose them, but that is documented. This is documented architectural intent, not a bug.
candidates.remaining_check: Verify UI handles missing journal gracefully when user clicks a ghost session
candidates.original_candidate_title: 3. Invalid UTF-8 in a torn append fails the entire journal, not one line
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `index_journal_file` (`indexer.rs`) uses `std::fs::read_to_string(path)?`. Any invalid UTF-8 returns `Err`, which `index_all` treats as `failed` (no row, or stale row left in place). Line-level `serde_json` skip only runs after a successful UTF-8 read. `spawn_writer` uses `writeln!(file, "{line}")` with no `sync_all`; on disk-full / kill it still continues (`note_write_error` does not stop the loop).

candidates.title: busy_timeout=2000 may cause SQLITE_BUSY under heavy re-index + UI query load
candidates.rationale: busy_timeout=2000ms is set at line 49. If the indexer holds a write lock for >2s (large batch of sessions), concurrent reads from the archive UI could fail with SQLITE_BUSY. WAL mode allows concurrent reads during writes normally, but the write transaction in replace_session deletes+reinserts all rows for a session, which can block checkpointing.
candidates.counterevidence: WAL mode specifically allows concurrent reads while writing. SQLITE_BUSY under WAL is rare — it occurs mainly during WAL checkpoint, not normal writes. The indexer processes one session at a time (replace_session), not bulk batches. 2000ms is a generous timeout for single-session transactions. No user reports of SQLITE_BUSY errors found.

Independently, `chars().take(MAX_ITEM_CHARS)` (`context_builder.rs` 72; `summary_ref.rs` 163) and uncapped `NewMemoryCandidate.text` (`candidates.rs` 88–89, `format!("Q: {}\nA: {}", …)` with only `MIN_ANSWER_CHARS=80`, no max) truncate at prompt build.

candidates.title: rank_by_relevance falls back to recency — may surface stale facts over relevant ones
candidates.rationale: When zero keyword matches are found (or no query is provided), rank_by_relevance degrades to newest-first recency ordering. This may surface recently-added but irrelevant facts over older relevant ones.
candidates.counterevidence: The test relevant_old_fact_beats_newer_noise confirms that when keywords DO match, relevance beats recency. The recency fallback is the graceful degradation for queries with no matching terms — surfacing recent context is a reasonable default. MAX_ITEMS=8 bounds the impact.
candidates.remaining_check: None — documented design choice with test coverage
candidates.original_candidate_title: 6. Unconditional recency fallback leaks private facts into unrelated asks
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `context_for_meeting` (`context_builder.rs` 180–202): `rank_by_relevance` returns `None` when `query_terms` is empty (`≥4` chars after `STOPWORDS`, 109–117) or score=0 (139–147); caller then `format_memory_block(&items)` — newest 8 **always**. `query_terms` drops short identifiers (`Go`, `Ян`, `S3`, 3-letter names).

candidates.title: summary_reference key_terms extraction misses lowercase technical terms
candidates.rationale: key_terms extracts capitalized words, ALL-CAPS tokens, Latin terms in Cyrillic text, and definition subjects. Lowercase technical terms (e.g., 'kubernetes', 'docker') would not be extracted as key terms, so memory items about them would not be gated into the summary reference.
candidates.counterevidence: The gating is intentionally conservative — it prevents irrelevant memory items from polluting meeting summaries. The summary path is a REFERENCE addition, not the primary context. If a term appears in the transcript, the transcript itself provides the context. The memory reference only adds decode-help for proper nouns and acronyms.
candidates.remaining_check: None — conservative design intent
candidates.original_candidate_title: 7. Summary term heuristic over-matches (stem and short Latin)
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `term_in_tokens` (`summary_ref.rs` 130–140): terms with `n>=5` use `stem = term[0..n-1]` and `tokens.iter().any(|t| t.starts_with(&stem))`. `key_terms` marks `latin_in_cyrillic` with **no minimum length** (90–93, 107): any ASCII alnum token in a Cyrillic fact (including `in`, `on`, `at`, `Go`).

candidates.title: extract_heuristic may produce cross-session near-duplicate candidates
candidates.rationale: Duplicate with C12 from persistence report. The dedup uses exact text comparison via candidate_texts(). Cross-session near-duplicates (same Q&A with slightly different STT output) produce separate candidates.
candidates.counterevidence: Same as C12 — known limitation of heuristic extraction. User reviews and approves/rejects candidates manually.
candidates.remaining_check: None
candidates.original_candidate_title: 8. Full-table load + nested tokenize/score on every ask; no fact dedup
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `open_default_store` + `list_memory_items("default", false, -1)` (`context_builder.rs` 186–189; `summary_ref.rs` 181–184) materializes **all** active rows. `rank_by_relevance` tokenizes every item+entity per term (`score_item` 119–132) and `clone()`s winners (162–164). `format_memory_block` / `format_summary_reference` do not dedupe by `id` or normalized text. `candidates.rs` `answer_candidates` dedupes questions only via whitespace+lowercase (`normalize` 160–165), not semantic clones; `topic_candidates` is `HashMap` over all question tokens (99–147). Comment admits FTS5 only at ~150–200 items (`context_builder.rs` 137–138).

candidates.title: POSIX credentials_path() creates suflyor/, poisoning data_root() away from overlay-mvp
candidates.rationale: On non-Windows (macOS), posix_credentials creates ~/.config/suflyor/ via ensure_dir_permissions → create_dir_all. data_root_in checks if the brand dir ('suflyor') exists before falling back to legacy ('overlay-mvp'). If credentials are accessed before migrate_data_root(), the empty suflyor/ dir makes data_root_in return it, skipping the legacy dir where actual data resides. migrate_data_root() then sees brand.exists()=true and returns AlreadyDone without migrating.
candidates.counterevidence: In practice, app_bootstrap.rs:14 calls migrate_data_root() BEFORE any credential access during normal startup. The race requires credential access from a code path that runs before bootstrap, which doesn't exist in the current call graph. However, the coupling between two modules via a shared directory name is fragile and could break if startup order changes. The product primarily targets Windows where Credential Manager is used (no filesystem dir). On macOS, credentials_path uses config_dir (typically ~/.config/suflyor/) while data_root uses data_dir/config_dir — need to verify these are the same directory on macOS.
candidates.remaining_check: Verify whether macOS dirs::config_dir and the data_root base directory are actually the same path
candidates.original_candidate_title: 1. POSIX `credentials_path()` creates `suflyor/`, poisoning `data_root()` away from `overlay-mvp`
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `posix_credentials::credentials_path()` (`credentials.rs`) always does `dirs::config_dir()?.join("suflyor")` + `ensure_dir_permissions()` → `create_dir_all`. `paths::data_root_in()` then treats **any** existing brand dir as authoritative (`if !brand.exists() && legacy.exists() { legacy } else { brand }`). Credential I/O therefore materializes an empty brand tree and silently orphans a still-populated `overlay-mvp` tree (config, sessions, recordings, keys in `config.json`).

candidates.title: Config export includes live secrets (ai_bearer, groq_api_key)
candidates.rationale: export_to calls portable_config_bytes which serializes the full Config, only removing deep_lock. The ai_bearer, groq_api_key, stt_whisper_bearer, hermes_bridge_token and other legacy secrets are included in the exported file. secret_redacted() exists (line 1632) but is NOT called by export_to.
candidates.counterevidence: This is BY DESIGN — the export is intended to transfer the user's complete configuration including credentials to another machine. The import_from function restores these credentials. The user explicitly triggers export via the Settings UI. However, the exported file contains plaintext secrets that could be inadvertently shared.
candidates.remaining_check: None — design intent confirmed; the report correctly identifies that export contains secrets
candidates.original_candidate_title: 2. `mask_host` keeps query, fragment, and “path-as-authority” bytes (token / LAN IP leaks)
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `mask_host` (`config.rs`) splits authority only on the first `/`, `?`, or `#`, then emits `format!("{scheme}***{port}{path}")` **verbatim**. It never redacts `path`/`query`/`fragment`. Scheme-relative and extra-slash URLs make the host fall into `path`.

candidates.title: Config save is not truly atomic on all filesystems
candidates.rationale: save_to_path uses write-to-temp + rename pattern (lines 1563-1618). The code comments state 'rename within the same directory is atomic on NTFS'. This is correct for NTFS but the rename is NOT atomic on all POSIX filesystems under all conditions (e.g., NFS, some network mounts). However, the app stores config in local %APPDATA% or ~/.config/.
candidates.counterevidence: The temp file is in the same directory as the target (sibling temp file), so the rename is on the same filesystem. On NTFS (primary target) and HFS+/APFS (macOS), rename within the same directory is atomic. The preserve_corrupt_config function (line 1390) provides additional safety by preserving unparseable configs before falling back to defaults. This is a robust implementation for the target platforms.
candidates.remaining_check: None — correct for target platforms
candidates.original_candidate_title: 3. Diagnostics `readiness()` embeds unmasked LAN URLs and OS-username paths
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `Config::readiness()` (`config.rs`) builds UI `detail` with raw `ep.base_url` (`format!("{} · {} · {}", provider, ep.base_url, ep.model)`), raw `stt_gigaam_dir`, and raw `stt_whisper_url`. It never calls `mask_host`. `preview_server_settings()` likewise copies `ai_base_url` / `openai_base_url` / `vision_base_url` / `stt_whisper_url` / `stt_gigaam_dir` into `PreviewGroup` / `gigaam_dir_*` without masking.

candidates.title: preserve_corrupt_config renames to .broken-<unix_secs> — collision if called twice in same second
candidates.rationale: The backup filename uses unix_secs (1-second granularity). Two corrupt config loads in the same second would try to rename to the same backup filename. The second rename would overwrite the first backup.
candidates.counterevidence: Config load happens once at startup. Two loads in the same second would require the app to crash and restart within one second, then encounter a corrupt config again. This is an extremely unlikely scenario. Even if it occurred, the most recent corrupt file is preserved (overwriting the earlier one from the same second).
candidates.remaining_check: None — negligible practical risk
candidates.original_candidate_title: 4. `config.json.bak` is world-readable; `config.json.broken-*` keeps live secrets forever
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `save_to_path` writes the undo snapshot with `std::fs::write(&bak, redacted)` (no `mode(0o600)`), while the live file is opened with `.mode(0o600)` only on the Unix tmp path. `preserve_corrupt_config` `rename`s the unparseable file to `config.json.broken-<unix_secs>` with **no** `secret_redacted()`, **no** chmod, **no** retention cap.

candidates.title: serde default fallback for missing fields may silently reset user preferences
candidates.rationale: Config fields use #[serde(default)] extensively. If a config.json is loaded from a newer version that added a field, then re-saved by an older version, the field is lost. The report claims this could silently reset user preferences.
candidates.counterevidence: This is standard serde behavior and is the correct approach for forward/backward compatibility. The alternative (strict deserialization) would cause config load failures on version upgrade. The preserve_corrupt_config mechanism handles truly unparseable configs. Users upgrading versions would see new fields initialized to defaults, which is the expected UX.
candidates.remaining_check: None — standard serde pattern
candidates.original_candidate_title: 5. POSIX credentials dir/file TOCTOU and tmp symlink follow
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `ensure_dir_permissions` is `create_dir_all` then `metadata` then conditional `set_permissions(0o700)` — not `open(O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW)` + `fchmod`. `write_to_path` does `path.with_extension("tmp")` (`credentials.json` → **`credentials.tmp`**), `OpenOptions::new().create(true).truncate(true).mode(0o600).open(&tmp)` (follows symlinks), then `rename`.

candidates.title: readiness report does not check network or audio — gives false confidence
candidates.rationale: Config::readiness() (line 957) builds a ReadinessReport from config fields only (line 712-724 doc: 'Config-only (no network / no audio) readiness snapshot'). It checks whether API keys are present, endpoints are configured, etc., but does not verify network connectivity or audio device availability.
candidates.counterevidence: The doc explicitly states 'Config-only (no network / no audio)' and 'the live AI/STT pings are layered on top' (line 724). The readiness report is one layer of a multi-layer diagnostics system. Live pings are performed separately. This is not a false confidence issue — it's a documented scope limitation.
candidates.remaining_check: None — documented scope limitation
candidates.original_candidate_title: 6. Direct-provider secrets are copied into owned `String`s with no zeroization (Windows blob included)
candidates.original_claim_redacted: Windows `read` does `bytes.to_vec()` + `String::from_utf8` then `CredFree` without wiping `CredentialBlob`. Windows `write` zeroizes only the local `blob` via `fill(0)` after `CredWriteW` (not on unwind, not the `CREDENTIALW` copy). POSIX `read_map` / `write` keep a `HashMap<String, String>` and `cloned()` values. `protected_provider_secret` returns that `String` into `AiEndpoint.bearer` on every `ai_endpoint()` / `vision_endpoint()` / `readiness()` call. `secret_redacted` `clone()`s the whole `Config` then `clear()`s secret fields (capacity retained, plaintext left in the clone’s buffers until drop).

candidates.title: server settings import can overwrite local AI configuration
candidates.rationale: import_server_settings applies selective fields from imported config to current config. The function at line 1693-1698 transfers cloud AI provider/endpoint settings. The preview_server_settings_from function (line 2033) shows the user what would change before applying.
candidates.counterevidence: The import has a preview step (preview_server_settings_from) that shows a REDACTED diff before applying. The user explicitly confirms the import. The import is selective (only server-related fields), not a full overwrite. This is a feature, not a vulnerability.
candidates.remaining_check: None — preview + explicit confirmation is adequate
candidates.original_candidate_title: 7. POSIX credentials RMW is non-atomic: corrupt JSON or concurrent writers drop the other slot
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `write`/`delete` do `read_map()` → mutate one key → `write_map()`. `read_map` on missing/unreadable/invalid JSON returns `HashMap::new()` (`unwrap_or_default()`), not an error. There is no file lock, `O_EXCL`, or merge.

candidates.title: http_error_line still takes op parameter from call site — could include URL
candidates.rationale: The report claims the op parameter could include a URL. Inspecting all call sites: stream.rs:221 passes 'AI stream', completion.rs:259 passes 'AI complete', inspect.rs:126 passes 'AI bridge test', inspect.rs:180 passes 'list_models', stt.rs:948 passes 'STT'. ALL call sites use hardcoded string literals, never URLs or dynamic content.
candidates.counterevidence: Every caller passes a static string literal. The function signature takes &str but the convention is enforced by code review. The test never_carries_body_text (line 33-46) validates that no body text leaks. The report's concern is speculative and not supported by the actual codebase.
candidates.remaining_check: None — all callers verified
candidates.original_candidate_title: 8. `import_server_settings_from` clobbers machine-local `stt_gigaam_dir` (path / username / traversal)
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `merge_server_settings` copies `imported.stt_gigaam_dir` (and `stt_gigaam_gpu`) onto `current`. `import_server_settings_from` saves that merge directly. `apply_server_settings` (the documented UI Apply path) explicitly **reverts** `stt_gigaam_dir` because it is a path on this PC. Preview even surfaces `gigaam_dir_incoming` as “NOT applied”.

candidates.title: POSIX credential file permissions 0o700 on dir but file permissions unverified
candidates.rationale: ensure_dir_permissions (line 124-135) sets 0o700 on the directory. The file write uses OpenOptionsExt with mode(0o600) for the temp file (write_map_to). However, the report questions whether the final file (after rename from temp) retains 0o600 permissions.
candidates.counterevidence: On POSIX, rename preserves the source file's permissions. The temp file is created with mode(0o600), so after rename it retains 0o600. The test at line 278-280 verifies directory permissions (0o700). The file creation uses explicit mode setting via OpenOptionsExt.
candidates.remaining_check: Verify the umask interaction — if umask is more restrictive, the file may get tighter permissions than 0o600
candidates.original_candidate_title: 9. Load/save error paths log filesystem paths (OS username) and default-write can persist a wiped config
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `config_path()` uses `.with_context(|| format!("create config dir {}", dir.display()))`. `load()` logs `config dir unavailable ({e})`, `config read failed ({e})`, and `preserved corrupt config as {}` with `backup.display()`. `data_root()` is `%APPDATA%\<user>\…` / `$HOME/…`. After parse failure, `preserve_corrupt_config` + `Config::defaults()`; if any migration sets `dirty`, `save(&cfg)` writes **defaults** over the canonical path.

candidates.title: http_error_line op parameter should have a negative test for URL injection
candidates.rationale: The report suggests adding a negative test that verifies http_error_line with a URL-like op string is rejected. This is a testing recommendation, not a finding of an existing defect.
candidates.counterevidence: All existing callers use static string literals (verified above in C08). The function itself is a simple format! macro that doesn't validate its inputs. Adding a negative test would be defense-in-depth but the current code has no vulnerability. The report's suggestion is a quality improvement, not a security finding.
candidates.remaining_check: None — this is a testing recommendation, not a defect
candidates.original_candidate_title: 10. `http_error_line` is safe in isolation; `op` is an unsanitized injection point
candidates.original_claim_redacted: `http_error_line(op, status, body_len)` (`http_log.rs`) interpolates `op` with no host/userinfo/query stripping and never receives the URL or body. Callers outside this file that pass `format!("{url}")` or status-text into `op` reintroduce the P0-1 leak this helper was written to stop.
